title: Learning new tunes from records and Lehmann's Music Shop; 'Kid Scottie' and the Amsterdam
summary: He gets new records saved by Mr. Lehmann, learns numbers before the sheet music arrives, and is nicknamed Kid Scottie by older veterans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So on the job, if they got a new number to play, I knew it. They'd all say, hey, Scottie, where did you get that? How do you know this number? I wouldn't tell them. I said, I heard it, you know, like that. We lived uptown then, 131st Street, and 135th Street there was Lehmann's Music Shop. Well, to get all the accessories like mutes for my trumpet, and like that, I stopped there instead of having to go downtown.
I made friends with the old man Lehmann, the place is still there now, but it's mostly a card shop. The old man is dead, and his sons took over. He knew I was a musician, because
most of the time I was in a tuxedo. I used to come from high school, change my clothes, put on a tuxedo and then meet the fellows at the Amsterdam.

And we'd go out there. Well, they saw me there and they knew I was a musician. So all the records that came -- the new records from the shows and things, Mr. Lehmann used to save them for me. I'd take them home, play them on the record. Get my horn out, I had it, see. When I went to work, I had that number before those fellows got the music sheets. I knew it. So when they played it, I was able to take my solo.

Well, well, well, I got another job -- I couldn't join the Amsterdam, I was too young. But I met all those old fellows, and most of them had been in World War I. And they used to call me Kid Scottie at that time. Well, I didn't mind, I was so happy to be playing music with them. And I got a lot of experience from them, and all like that.
